theorem: If every occurrence of each CNF variable is replaced by a fresh copy and all copies are joined by a connected variable-local equality gadget, while original clause nodes are retained, then the original variable-clause incidence graph is a minor of the transformed incidence graph.
consequence: By minor monotonicity of treewidth, this compiler pattern cannot reduce incidence treewidth.
proof_object: Pairwise-disjoint connected branch sets: one local copy/equality branch set per source variable and one singleton per source clause; every source incidence edge is witnessed by its clause-to-copy edge.

located_bottleneck.name: NON_MINOR_PRESERVING_SEMANTIC_COMPRESSION
located_bottleneck.definition: A universal low-width compiler must genuinely remove or semantically quotient source interactions, rather than merely subdividing them with definitional equality gadgets.

claim_boundary: This blocks one broad width-reduction pattern. It does not exclude semantic elimination, algebraic compression, or prove P!=NP.

references.authors: Neil Robertson and P. D. Seymour
references.title: Graph minors. II. Algorithmic aspects of tree-width
references.role: Treewidth and graph-minor framework used by the monotonicity consequence.
